pr_title: provider: flush the store cache when providers are loaded/unloaded.
pr_body:
When the providers change, the method cache needs to be flushed.

Fixes #15032

- [ ] documentation is added or updated
- [x] tests are added or updated
pr_comments: The fix isn't quite so easy as I thought ...

~This is likely dependent on a fix @mattcaswell has in another PR.~

I'm not so sure anymore.
Thanks @mattcaswell, I was thinking of deferring the flush but hadn't got to it yet which is exactly what isn't happening in your patch :grin:
Ahh looks like the flush you are doing is not working too well :) (You already have a test - for some reason I was looking at a single commit - not the PR).
I forgot I put the test in :(
I think `provider->operation_bits` also needs resetting when you flush the cache.

> I think provider->operation_bits also needs resetting when you flush the cache.

Hmmm...does that need to happen for *all* providers when we flush??

I've added the code to flush on first activate and final deactivate.  With this in, I'm not sure we need to do anything with `provider->operation_bits`.  It's either a new provider or about to disappear.
Why is it always `sslapitest` that causes problems :cry:

Just remove the test :)
That uses the XOR - probably related to that..

> With this in, I'm not sure we need to do anything with provider->operation_bits. It's either a new provider or about to disappear.

But if we've flushed the cache doesn't that mean that providers that are *not* changing will have their entries flushed - but they won't be queried again because of `operation_bits`?
Yes....
I don't think there is a sensible way to only flush the cache for a single provider.  Too many nasties lurking.

> I don't think there is a sensible way to only flush the cache for a single provider. Too many nasties lurking.

Which implies you have to reset `operation_bits` for all providers.
I would expect provider load/unload to be quite heavy operation that should not be done "just in case". Perhaps adding a note in documentation would be worth it though.
I think we've got a problem.  The `operation_bits` clearing will also need to happen on a partial cache flush which isn't happening either.
Needs a make update
I think I hate the FIPS checksum script already :laughing:
May be worth keeping an eye on it to see it actually works also for the files you change...
Fixing the `operatin_bits` resetting solved the sslapitest failure too.
CI's are relevant, excluding the FIPS checksum problem.

issue_context.title: Fetch calls return success for an unavailable provider
comments: There was a missing cache flush on unload.

review_comments: I suppose it does not matter that the count might not reflect the real current value.

In this case it shouldn't, the provider won't go deactivated during this call but it could be activated again but that won't flush since the count would be 2.

I am worried that there are race conditions in the provider/store/fetch code.  There are a lot of different locks involved and after any unlock there is window where things might change.  For the moment, I'll call it a bout of _paranoia_.
